rationale: System documentation is the control the commit plane reads better than the runtime source does, and it is the shape of the argument for most of the SA family: administrator and user documentation describing secure configuration, installation, operation and effective use is a set of documents, and a repository is a document store under version control with authorship, review and a content hash per commit. rampscan can evidence that the documents exist at named paths, that they are non-empty, when they last changed, which commit changed them and who reviewed that change — the existence, currency and integrity half of the control, anchored the same way every other claim here is anchored.

remainder.control: Distribution: the control requires the documentation to reach defined personnel or roles, and no commit records that anyone received or read it — the same gap upstream names for every policy control, and it is not closed by the document being public.
remainder.boundary: And the repository set. This scan read one checkout; whether it holds all the system documentation inside the authorization boundary — or the administrator guide lives in a second repository nobody pointed rampscan at — is named by a human, not by any commit. An evidenced result here means the documents named at these paths are current, never that the documentation set is complete.

externalSystem: Nothing. Collectors take no network by decision, execution is local, and signing is node:crypto. The documentation is read from the checkout in place; no document is uploaded to a service to be indexed, which is the usual route by which a documentation control quietly acquires an external system.
